I kind of agree with this general statement. It is definitely about efficient order. but I disagree with your analysis of the mechanics of adjective priority. If you look at the order of the adjective list: opinion, size, age-shape-color-origin-material-purpose... what seems significant to me is that it's basically going from words of general applicability to specific applicability.

Just imagine all the things in your house for a second. Imagine you get just two adjectives to try to figure out what someone is looking for in your house. Knowing the thing is lovely and little doesn't eliminate as many potential things in your house as knowing something rectangular and green, and similarly knowing something is french and made of silver eliminates even more things than rectangular and green does.

Taking a look at the adjective list order again.... purpose, when compared to the rest of the adjective categories, is very much specifically tied or inseparable to/from he the thing in question. Purpose comes last, closest to the noun. No back to the first word, opinion, It makes sense that opinion would come first under this analysis. Opinions aren't very tied to specific things. Your opinion on some things can change from second to second.

TLDR: The adjective order goes from adjective categories of general applicability to specific applicability. Or in other words, the adjectives closest to the word are the descriptors most categorically tied to the noun in question.
